answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to post a bond and earn reputation through repeated, independently checked transactions. Random agents audit claims, and a consensus failure slashes the bond while reducing future access to profitable work. A genuine identity accumulates trust gradually, like a terrace built stone by stone; a fake network must finance each sparrow separately, and one exposed inconsistency can send a ripple through linked accounts, destroying its capital and reputation.
